Q: Creating functions (or lambdas) in a loop (or comprehension) A:

You're running into a problem with late binding -- each function looks up i as late as possible (thus, when called after the end of the loop, i will be set to 2).

Easily fixed by forcing early binding: change def f(): to def f(k=i): like this:

def f(k=i):
    return k

Default values (the i in k=i is a default value for argument name k) are looked up at def time, not at call time, so essentially they're a way to do early binding.

If you're worried about f getting an extra argument (and thus potentially being called erroneously), there's a more sophisticated way which involves using a closure as a "function factory":

def make_f(k):
    def f():
        return k
    return f

and in your loop use f = make_f(i) instead of the def statement.

for i in range(3):
    f = make_f(i)
    functions.append(f)

Q: Where are Visual Studio Code log files? A:

Workaround: "Open Output In Editor"

For extension logs, I couldn't find any actual log files that were created for certain extensions. But I noticed that for anything under the "OUTPUT" window you can:

  • Click three dots on right
  • Open Output in Editor

which opens the current log in an editor window which allows you to sanely browse it.

There are other options of interest in that menu:

  • Save output as: saves only the current log window to a file
  • Export Logs...: allows you to select any number of log files to export all at once in a single ZIP

Tested on VS Code 1.107.1.
